references.title: Nightmare mode: simulating disk failures
references.text: Antithesis ran a patched LazyFS on customer workloads, where it found subtle data-loss bugs.

references.title: VoltDB Jepsen tests
references.text: VoltDB added LazyFS power-loss and torn-write scenarios to its Jepsen test suite.

references.title: SpacetimeDB: un-fsync'd writes
references.text: Jepsen tests on LazyFS found unsynced files and silent data loss after simulated power failures; fixed in October 2026.

references.title: ArcadeDB 26.11.1
references.text: Crash-safety bugs fixed in this release were found by a Jepsen + LazyFS power-loss sweep.

references.title: ParticleDB 1.1.4
references.text: The test harness simulated the loss of un-fsynced writes using LazyFS.

references.title: NATS 2.12.1
references.text: Jepsen's tests “relied heavily on LazyFS”: simulated power failures lost acknowledged JetStream writes.

references.title: Capela dda5892
references.text: Capela ran on LazyFS, combining forgotten un-fsynced data with process crashes.

references.title: DuckDB: Analytics-Optimized Concurrent Transactions
references.text: DuckDB re-ran its write-ahead-log crash and durability tests on LazyFS.

references.title: MySQL 8.0.34
references.text: The first public Jepsen report using LazyFS, which Jepsen commissioned from INESC TEC in 2022.

references.title: etcd robustness tests
references.text: etcd installs LazyFS in CI so its robustness tests can lose un-fsynced writes.

references.title: MongoDB WiredTiger
references.text: The WiredTiger storage engine extended its fault-injection tests to run on LazyFS.

references.title: Jepsen: jepsen.lazyfs
references.text: Lets any Jepsen test run on LazyFS; used by the etcd, MongoDB, MySQL, NATS and other test suites.
